business_model.claim: Yalla Group Limited operates a mobile social networking and gaming platform where users access basic group chatting functions for free and can purchase virtual currencies to buy virtual items, upgrade services, or play games.
quotes: We operate a social networking and gaming platform using a revenue model whereby users can get free access to the basic functions on the platform for our group chatting service but have the options to purchase virtual currencies.
Individual users consume virtual currencies to purchase virtual items and upgrade services or play games on our platform.

business_model.claim: The platform sells virtual items consisting mainly of virtual gifts and chat room or game privileges, along with upgrade services such as VIP rights or premium memberships, none of which are convertible into real money or resalable between users.
quotes: Virtual items primarily consist of various virtual gifts and privileges in chat rooms or games.
Upgrade services primarily consist of VIP rights or premium membership on our platform.

While our users may receive virtual gifts and accumulate virtual currencies on our platform, none of the virtual gifts and virtual currencies are convertible into real money under any circumstance and our users are unable to sell such virtual items to other users through our platform.

business_model.claim: The company serves individual users primarily in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), particularly Arabic-speaking users, with products localized to regional customs and offline social leisure traditions.
quotes: A substantial number of our users are Arabic-speaking, and activities on our platform mirror popular offline social leisure activities in MENA.

In addition, we launched three more casual game mobile applications targeting different regions, namely Yalla Baloot, a card game designed for Saudi Arabian users, 101 Okey Yalla, a board game designed for Turkish users, and Yalla Parchis, a South American version of Yalla Ludo.

business_model.claim: Although Yalla has added Yalla Game Limited for mid-core and hard-core games alongside Yalla Baloot, 101 Okey Yalla, Yalla Parchis, YallaChat, and WeMuslim, its two flagship apps—Yalla and Yalla Ludo—still contribute the majority of revenues.
quotes: We operate two flagship mobile applications, Yalla, a voice-centric group chat platform, and Yalla Ludo, a casual gaming application featuring online versions of board games popular in MENA, with in-game voice chat and localized majlis functions.

Though we expect that these various new products will enable us to further diversify our revenue streams in the future, currently our flagship mobile applications, Yalla and Yalla Ludo, still contribute to the majority of our revenues.

business_model.claim: Revenues are directly affected by paying users and ARPPU: in the fourth quarter of 2025 paying users fell from 12.3 million to 10.4 million due to fewer third-party payment platform promotions while ARPPU rose from US$7.2 to US$7.9, before paying users increased 6.2% year over year to 12.1 million in the third quarter of 2026.
quotes: Our revenues are primarily affected by the number of paying users and ARPPU.

The number of paying users decreased from 12.3 million for the fourth quarter of 2024 to 10.4 million for the fourth quarter of 2025, primarily due to fewer promotion events held by third-party payment platforms in the same period.

Our ARPPU increased from US$7.2 in the fourth quarter of 2024 to US$7.9 in the same period of 2025 mainly because our enhanced social and gamification features derive users to spend more on our platform.

business_model.claim: Because the platform centers on user-to-user interactions, the company avoids significant content acquisition costs such as incentive fees to key users or media content purchases, while benefiting from organic word-of-mouth user referrals.
quotes: As our platform promotes users’ interactions, we do not incur significant content acquisition cost, such as incentive fees to key users or costs for acquiring media content.
We benefit from organic user acquisition through word-of-mouth referrals, and we will also continue to focus on cost-effective user acquisition channels to manage selling and marketing expenses.

business_model.claim: Cost of revenues consists mainly of third-party payment platform commission fees and platform operations staff costs, decreasing 7.1% from US$120.5 million in 2024 to US$111.9 million in 2025 primarily because diversified payment channels lowered commission fees by US$4.9 million.
quotes: Our cost of revenues consists primarily of (i) commission fees paid to third party payment platforms and (ii) staff cost and expenses related to the operations of our mobile platform.

Our cost of revenues decreased by 7.1% from US$120.5 million in 2024 to US$111.9 million in 2025, mainly due to lower commission fees paid to third-party payment platforms by US$4.9 million from 2024 to 2025 as a result of diversified payment channels.

business_model.claim: Selling and marketing expenses are driven primarily by advertising and market promotion alongside staff, rental, and depreciation costs, increasing 10.2% from US$31.3 million in 2024 to US$34.6 million in 2025 as advertising and promotion rose US$7.3 million, and doubling year over year in the second quarter of 2026 to promote new products.
quotes: Our selling and marketing expenses consist primarily of (i) advertising costs and market promotion expenses and (ii) staff cost, rental and depreciation related to selling and marketing functions.

Our selling and marketing expenses increased by 10.2% from US$31.3 million in 2024 to US$34.6 million in 2025, mainly due to an increase in advertising and market promotion expenses by US$7.3 million from 2024 to 2025 attributable to our continued user acquisition efforts and expanding product portfolio, and partially offset by a decrease of US$2.9 million in salaries and benefits for our selling and marketing staff.
While doubling our selling and marketing expenses year over year to support the promotion of new products, we maintained a healthy non-GAAP net margin of 41.7% through increased efficiency.

business_model.claim: Technology and product development expenses consist mainly of staff and related costs for designing new platform features and self-developed games, growing 18.0% from US$29.0 million in 2024 to US$34.3 million in 2025 on a US$5.4 million rise in staff salaries and benefits from headcount expansion.
quotes: Our technology and product development expenses consist primarily of (i) staff cost and (ii) related expenses for the employees involved in designing and developing new features for our mobile platform and self-developed mobile games.

Our technology and product development expenses increased by 18.0% from US$29.0 million in 2024 to US$34.3 million in 2025, mainly due to an increase in salaries and benefits for our technology and product development staff by US$5.4 million from 2024 to 2025, driven by an increase in the headcount of our technology and product development staff to support the development of new businesses and expansion of our product portfolio.

business_model.claim: General and administrative expenses consist primarily of staff costs, rental, depreciation, professional service fees, and corporate expenses, rising 4.1% from US$37.4 million in 2024 to US$39.0 million in 2025 mainly due to a US$2.1 million increase in foreign exchange loss.
quotes: Our general and administrative expenses consist primarily of (i) staff cost, rental and depreciation related to general and administrative personnel, (ii) professional service fees and (iii) other corporate expenses.
The increase was mainly due to an increase in foreign exchange loss of US$2.1 million from 2024 to 2025.

growth_thesis.basis: stated in the cited items (MAU figures and growth percentages are directly reported in P2, P3, and P4)
growth_thesis.claim: User base expansion is a core growth driver: average MAUs increased by 14.4% to 41.4 million in the fourth quarter of 2024, by 8.2% to 44.8 million in the fourth quarter of 2025, and by 12.3% year-over-year to 47.6 million in the second quarter of 2026, reaching 47,241 (table in thousands) in the third quarter of 2026.

Average MAUs have grown rapidly, primarily due to continued efforts in user acquisition to penetrate the market.

Meanwhile, our core products continued to build momentum, with refined operations and targeted marketing driving a sequential rebound in paying users for Yalla Ludo and a 12.3% year-over-year increase in overall average MAUs to 47.6 million.

quotes: We seek to further expand our user base by penetrating our existing markets and expanding into other underserved markets.

Our ability to expand user base depends on our abilities to, among other things, deliver superior user experience, raise brand recognition, utilize cost-effective user acquisition channels and increase attractiveness and breadth of content offerings.

growth_thesis.basis: stated in the cited items (P2 reports ARPPU figures and attributes the rise to social and gamification features)

Our ARPPU increased from US$7.2 in the fourth quarter of 2024 to US$7.9 in the same period of 2025 mainly because our enhanced social and gamification features derive users to spend more on our platform.

growth_thesis.basis: stated in the cited item (P2 identifies conversion, activity, virtual items, and upgrade services as monetization drivers and notes the effect of fewer third-party promotions)

Revenues generated from games services in the third quarter of 2026 were US$38.4 million.

growth_thesis.basis: inferred from P1, P2, and P4 (flagship concentration in P1, rising R&D expense share in P2, and doubled marketing expense with lower GAAP net income in P4)
